subject.title: fix: keep tail alive after handler failures

question: Which handler failures may remain nonfatal, and when must repeated or systemic failures terminate the tail or mark it unhealthy?
rationale: The PR intentionally changes the tail's operational failure contract, but source alone cannot determine the acceptable event-loss window or whether supervisors depend on Tail returning for recovery.

options.title: Add bounded escalation
options.body: Continue after isolated failures, but terminate or report an unhealthy state after classified systemic errors or a bounded sequence of consecutive failures.

options.title: Accept all failures as event-scoped
options.body: Merge the blanket continuation behavior and explicitly document that operators must monitor warnings and repair missed events independently.

recommendation.title: Add bounded escalation
recommendation.body: Continue after isolated failures, but terminate or report an unhealthy state after classified systemic errors or a bounded sequence of consecutive failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal ties this person to the original internal tail architecture and its failure contract.
